title: acme-orders: take-over
subtitle: The take-over chain on acme-orders: each step's page, what it found, what is still open, and whether the chain is done.

verdict.text: The chain ran all five steps and the repository is mapped, audited and documented, but it is not safe to own yet: the daily import has been failing for five weeks on a parsing change nobody noticed. Fix that first, with the test test-gap named.

sections.title: The chain
sections.intro: Every step ran today; none was reused from an earlier day.

items.title: codebase-map · 2026-11-11 · risk
items.text: A small Python CLI; the daily import has failed since 2026-10-02 because decimal-comma parsing was removed.

items.title: code-audit · 2026-11-11 · risk
items.text: Four high findings, three in the import path; the pricing rounds twice.

items.title: dependency-audit · 2026-11-11 · watch
items.text: One reachable vulnerability in the mail client; two pins older than a year.

items.title: test-gap · 2026-11-11 · watch
items.text: Importer and pricing untested; two tests assert nothing.

items.title: docs-draft · 2026-11-11 · ok
items.text: Onboarding guide written from the four pages; the cron job outside the repo is marked as a guess.

blocks.text: **Rule:** The chain is done when all five pages exist from this run and validate. **Answer:** yes, five pages, all valid.

items: Fix the decimal-comma parsing and add the regression test test-gap wrote first (code-audit finding 1).
Upgrade the mail client in dependency-audit's first wave.
Ask finance who owns the nightly database copy, then close docs-draft's open item.
